Random traders will recognize ETH faster, a more erudite audience will likely prefer Ether. A non-technical generalist audience encountering Ethereum for the first time. It sounds like Ether would be the more formal or official version. Yeah. Like saying "United States Dollar" instead of "USD". If your audience is unfamiliar with the shorthand, it is better to use the long form. Especially in this case, since the long form is only 2 characters longer. Perhaps it's a matter of language or regions. But here, the very few people with whom I've spoken about this. Refer colloquially to Ether the token as "Ethereum" as a countable noun, eg "I just sold two Ethereums". I know it's wrong, just pointing out that "Ether" may throw some people off Excellent, thanks <@!301186049323958275> I will definitely make clear the correct way to distinguish them.
